whoWeAre.p1: Designs and manufactures blown-film lines, bag-making converters, and recycling systems for polymer film processors across six continents. Founded in 2008, we have grown from a single machine type to a full portfolio of 18+ machine families — every product designed in-house, fabricated in our 12,000 m² Wenzhou facility, and tested before it ships.
whoWeAre.p2: Our customers range from single-line converters running one shift a day to multi-site groups running 24/7 on four continents. The machine has to work the same way for both.

story.title: From one line to a full machinery portfolio
story.p1: Ashal Innomach started with a single-layer blown-film line and a small team of mechanical engineers who had spent the previous decade on the shop floors of Wenzhou's established machinery makers. The founding premise was simple: build fewer machine types, but build them better.
story.p2: Today we produce eighteen machine families across blown film, bag making, and recycling. Every product is designed in-house, fabricated in our 12,000 m² Wenzhou facility, and tested before it ships.

items.e: Company founded in Wenzhou. First single-layer blown-film line.
ABA three-layer co-extrusion line. First export to Southeast Asia.
Bag-making division launched with the F-PRO bottom-seal converter.
CE certification. ABC multi-layer line certified for PBAT+PLA.
CX recycling line released. Factory expanded to 12,000 m².
ABCDE-2200 enters development. Offices in Germany & Vietnam.
ABCDE-2200 ships. RGB roll-bag machine updated.

values.title: Four things we never compromise on

items.b: Every machine starts on the drawing board, not the sales brochure. We over-engineer where it matters — drive trains, die heads, frame rigidity — and simplify everything else.
We supply spare parts and provide remote process support for every machine we have ever built. A ten-year-old line deserves the same attention as a new one.
Our lines run LDPE, LLDPE, HDPE, PP, PBAT+PLA and blends. We do not design for one resin family and leave the rest as an afterthought.
Buyers are welcome on the production floor at any stage of a build. We encourage factory acceptance tests and third-party inspection.

film-blowing.title: Extrusion & Screw
film-blowing.detail: Multi-screw co-extrusion feeds molten resin into the die head at controlled temperature zones.

film-blowing.title: Die Head & Bubble
film-blowing.detail: The film bubble forms above the die, cooled by the air ring for consistent gauge.

film-blowing.title: Haul-Off & Winding
film-blowing.detail: Collapsed film is drawn up the tower and wound into finished rolls.

bag-making.title: Unwind & Feeding
bag-making.detail: Photocell-tracked unwind feeds film into the machine at controlled tension.

bag-making.title: Sealing & Cutting
bag-making.detail: Heat-seal bars and rotary cutters form and separate each bag at speed.

bag-making.title: Control Panel
bag-making.detail: PLC touchscreen sets bag length, seal temperature and lane speed.

recycling.title: Crusher & Feeding
recycling.detail: Scrap film and edge trim are crushed and fed into the extruder at a controlled rate.

recycling.title: Screen Changer
recycling.detail: Auto screen-changer filters contamination without stopping the line.

recycling.title: Pelletizing Head
recycling.detail: Molten resin is cut into uniform pellets and cooled for reuse.

printing.title: Unwind & Registration
printing.detail: Web tension and registration marks are tracked before the film reaches the first print station.

printing.title: CI Print Drum
printing.detail: Each colour station transfers ink from the anilox roller onto the central impression drum.

printing.title: Drying & Rewind
printing.detail: Inline dryers set each colour before the finished print is wound onto the rewind shaft.

flexoPrintingPage.heroDescription: 2 to 8 printing colours. Web widths 500–2000 mm. Full servo gearless drive with ±0.1 mm registration on PE, PP, PET, BOPP, paper and non-woven substrates.
flexoPrintingPage.chooseColourAndWidth: Choose your colour count & web width
flexoPrintingPage.substrateDescription: Ceramic anilox rollers at 200–600 LPI deliver consistent ink transfer across thin film, paper and woven materials. Independent IR drying per colour station prevents back-bleed.
